content:
Hello everyone,

it is our pleasure to announce Bob DyLean, a framework for the symbolic analysis of cryptographic protocols, in Lean, in collaboration with @Cas Cremers (link to paper).

DyLean works in the symbolic model of cryptography, in which we prove that cryptographic protocols are secure against attackers that control the network (i.e. can drop, replay, and modify messages), but are restricted to only use cryptographic functions as black boxes (hence capture "logical attacks"). Tools that provide guarantees in the symbolic model (e.g. Tamarin or ProVerif) have seen great success in the industry, e.g. to analyze standards and deployed protocols (like TLS 1.3, the protocol you are using to securely connect to Zulip!)

DyLean builds on top of previous research which has been shown to scale to large protocols: its semantics are close to the ones from state-of-the-art and widely used symbolic tool Tamarin; its proof methodology builds on the one from DY*, which I previously developed, and used to analyze the secure group messaging protocol MLS.

DyLean improves on DY* on several aspects:

  • our semantics of the symbolic model are user-extensible, whereas semantics of DY* are hardcoded
  • our semantics of the symbolic model are cleanly separated from the proof methodology: whereas the semantics allow to formally write "this protocol has this security property" as a Lean theorem statement, the proof methodology is a means to convince Lean the theorem is true, but you could develop your own methodology!
  • on the proof methodology, we learn from the lessons of the biggest protocol analyzed with DY* (MLS) and improve on user experience and performance (we are still actively working on this)

GenAI disclaimer: this project did not use generative AI, the code is 100% organic and grass-fed :)

Théophile & Cas
